extracted.intended_audience: Entities applying for or holding FCC cable-landing licenses, carriers filing tariffs, and carrier compliance officers/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for applications, notifications, filings, reports, petitions, and routine conditions applicable to cable landing licensees, foreign carrier affiliations, and tariff-related filings under 47 CFR Part 1. Includes timing, content, service, and recordkeeping rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of cable landing license application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must include specified information required by §1.767(a), e.g., ownership, citizenship, organizational documents, narrative describing the cable, ownership diagrams, and certifications regarding foreign carrier affiliations and market power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must provide all information necessary for the Commission to act, including detailed ownership diagrams, identifying any entity owning >25% or controlling the applicant or a foreign carrier that controls the applicant. See §1.767(a)(1)–(11) for specific items; include any other information necessary to enable Commission action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign carrier ownership / control disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must disclose whether any entity owns more than 25 percent of the applicant, or controls the applicant, or controls a foreign carrier in that country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose identities of such entities and provide supporting documentation as part of the application (see §1.767(a)(8)(i)–(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate foreign carrier ownership contractual relation disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more foreign carriers (or parties controlling them) own >25% in the aggregate and are parties to or beneficiaries of contractual relations affecting provision/marketing, applicant must disclose that relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example contractual relations include joint ventures or market alliances affecting acquisition, sale, lease, transfer and use of capacity on the cable in the U.S. (see §1.767(a)(8)(D)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Market power demonstration for non‑WTO destination markets
rubrics_metrics.description: For any non‑WTO foreign country listed, applicant must demonstrate whether the foreign carrier lacks market power per §63.10(a) of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Commission presumes lack of market power if foreign carrier lacks 50% market share in relevant international transport/facilities/services, subject to rebuttal (see note to §1.767(a)(8)(iv) and §63.10(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of routine conditions certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must certify that it accepts and will abide by the routine conditions specified in paragraph (g) of §1.767.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine conditions include prior consent requirements for transfers, notification obligations, reporting duties, and other conditions in §1.767(g). See §1.767(a)(9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coastal Zone Management Act (CZMA) consistency certification obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for cable landing licenses may be subject to CZMA consistency certification requirements (16 U.S.C. 1456) if activities affect a state's coastal zone policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must consult NOAA regulations (15 CFR part 930, Subpart D), review state programs, follow procedures in 15 CFR 930.54 after filing, consult affected coastal states or OCRM for guidance, and include any required consistency certifications in the FCC application; update pursuant to §1.65 if later required (note to §1.767(a)(10)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment/transfer of control application content and diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying to assign or transfer control of an interest in a cable system, applicant must complete relevant application paragraphs for both transferor and transferee, include pre- and post-transaction ownership diagrams, a narrative of how transfer will occur, and segment‑specific percentages of voting and ownership interests transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the transferee needs to complete certain foreign-carrier-related items. Commission may request additional information for public-interest determination (see §1.767(a)(11)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to foreign carrier affiliation notification when transfer requires it
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transfer also requires filing a foreign carrier affiliation notification under §1.768, the application must reference that notification and its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.767(a)(11)(ii) and §1.768 for cross-reference requirements; also see §1.767(g)(7) re post‑transaction notification of pro forma assignments/transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑transaction notification timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee/transferee must notify the Commission no later than 30 days after consummation of the assignment or transfer, or a decision not to consummate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must identify the FCC file numbers under which the initial license and the authorization were granted (§1.767(a)(11)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate application per cable system
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate application is required for each individual cable system for license requests, modifications, renewals, or extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common carrier cable landing license applicants must also file a separate international section 214 authorization for overseas cable construction (§1.767(b)–(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior consent required for transfers (routine condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cable landing licenses and rights granted shall not be transferred, assigned, or disposed of (including indirect transfer by control) unless the FCC gives prior written consent, except as otherwise ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.767(g)(6) for the routine prior consent condition; exceptions provided in §1.767(g)(7) for pro forma transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma transfer/assignment notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma assignees/persons subject to a pro forma transfer of control need not seek prior approval but must notify the Commission no later than 30 days after consummation and certify the transaction was pro forma and does not change ultimate control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee may file a single notification for multiple licenses if each is identified by file number; definition of pro forma per §63.24 of this chapter (§1.767(g)(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of specific cable landing locations prior to construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless precise landing locations were specified in the application, the licensee must notify the Commission no later than 90 days prior to commencing construction at a landing location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission will give public notice and grant for that landing location is final unless it issues contrary notice within 60 days after receipt (§1.767(g)(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee must comply with §1.768 (foreign carrier affiliation notifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cable landing licensees must comply with the requirements of §1.768 regarding notifications and prior approvals for affiliations with foreign carriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.767(g)(12) and §1.768 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual international circuit capacity reporting obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees shall file annual international circuit capacity reports as required by §43.82 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.767(g)(13) for cross-reference to reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: In‑service notification and license term
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee must notify the Commission within 30 days after the cable is placed into service. The cable landing license expires 25 years from in‑service date unless renewed/extended; upon expiration all rights terminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.767(g)(15) for notification and term details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum applicants/licensees required on license
rubrics_metrics.description: At minimum, applicants/licensees must include any entity that owns or controls a U.S. cable landing station and all entities owning or controlling a 5% or greater interest using U.S. points of the cable system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.767(h)(1)–(2) for who must be an applicant/licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing and amendment requirements; relinquishment demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to pending applications and modification applications (including adding applicants/licensees) must be signed by each initial applicant/licensee or an appointed proxy. A licensee relinquishing interest must file a modification showing it is not required to be a licensee and remaining licensees will retain de jure/de facto control sufficient to comply with rules and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.767(m)(1)–(2) for signatures, proxies, and relinquishment demonstration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing via ICFS; submarine outage reports exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for submarine cable outage reports, all applications and notifications in this section must be filed electronically through the International Communications Filing System (ICFS), subject to availability of electronic forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICFS homepage lists available forms; see subpart Y; submarine cable outage reports filed per part 4 of this Title (§1.767(n)). See §§63.20 and 63.53 cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign carrier affiliation prior‑notification timing (§1.768)
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee must notify the Commission 45 days before consummation of transactions acquiring control of a foreign carrier or of >25% interests by/among licensee or foreign carrier, except as provided by §1.768(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.768(a)(1)–(2) for the two transaction types triggering prior notification; exceptions described in §1.768(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to prior notification (pre/post consummation filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification need not be filed before consummation if (1) Commission previously determined the foreign carrier lacks market power in that destination market, or (2) the foreign carrier owns no facilities in that market. Additional exceptions exist for WTO Member destinations if licensee demonstrates lack of market power per §63.10(a)(3) or commits to comply with reporting requirements in §1.767(l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.768(b)(1)–(2) and cross-references to §63.10(a)(3) and §1.767(l). Examples provided in §1.768(c) illustrate post‑consummation notification scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑consummation notification timing (§1.768(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a licensee becomes affiliated with a foreign carrier and has not previously notified the Commission, it must notify within 30 days after consummation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples clarify when post‑notification applies (e.g., acquisition >25% but not controlling; 100% acquisition if foreign carrier is resale carrier; acquisitions from WTO members may be post‑notification if subsequent demonstration or reporting commitment is made).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of foreign carrier affiliation notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification must certify: name of affiliated foreign carrier and countries where authorized/owns landing station; which are WTO members; cable system name and FCC file numbers; name/address/citizenship/principal business of any person owning ≥10% equity and percentage to nearest 1%; interlocking directorates; whether notification is under §1.768(a) or (c) and projected/actual closing date; and if relying on exceptions, the certification and citation to adjudications or required demonstrations/commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.768(e)(1)–(7) for the full list of required items and obligations to include demonstrations or certified commitments when relying on §1.768(b)(2) exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception from reporting requirements demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: If seeking to be excepted from reporting requirements in §1.767(l), licensee should demonstrate that each foreign carrier affiliate lacks market power pursuant to §63.10(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.768(f). This is a required demonstration to avoid reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and public comment on foreign carrier notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: After public notice of submissions under §1.768, interested parties may file comments within 14 days. Commission may impose reporting requirements based on §1.767(l) and may require public-interest showing or impose conditions if affiliation may harm public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.768(g)(1)–(2). Note 63.10(a) presumption re 50% market share applies (see note). Commission may proceed to authorization revocation hearing if required showing is not made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing accuracy and correction obligation for notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees are responsible for continuing accuracy of information provided for 45 days after filing; if information becomes inaccurate during that period, licensee must file corrected notification as promptly as possible and within 10 days unless good cause is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.768(h) for the 45-day responsibility and 10-day correction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary confidential treatment for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee filing a prior notification under §1.768(a) may request confidential treatment under §0.459 of this chapter for the first 20 days after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.768(i) for confidentiality timing and procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement for foreign affiliation notifications (ICFS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to availability of electronic forms, all §1.768 notifications must be filed electronically through ICFS; see §§1.1000–1.10018 and ICFS homepage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.768(j) and cross-references to §§63.20 and 63.53.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tariff filing construction and part 61 compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedules of charges, classifications, practices, and regulations required under section 203 of the Communications Act must be constructed, filed, and posted in accordance with part 61 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.771 for cross-reference to tariff construction and filing rules (part 61).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for special tariff permission form and manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications under section 203 for special tariff permission must be made in the form, manner, and number of copies set out in part 61 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.772 for cross-reference to procedural requirements in part 61.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for petitions to investigate/suspend/reject tariff filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions must specify the FCC tariff number and carrier transmittal number, the items protested, and specific reasons why the protested tariff filing warrants investigation, suspension, or rejection under the Communications Act; petitions cannot also be prayers to be treated as formal complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a single petition asks for more than one form of relief, each form of relief must be separately and distinctly pleaded and supported. See §1.773(a)(1) and (i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of showing required to suspend nondominant carrier tariffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Tariff filings by nondominant carriers are prima facie lawful and will not be suspended unless petition shows: (A) high probability the tariff would be found unlawful after investigation; (B) harm to competition would be more substantial than injury from unavailability of service under proposed rates; (C) irreparable injury will result if not suspended; and (D) suspension would not otherwise be contrary to the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the four‑part showing required under §1.773(a)(1)(ii). Similar four‑part showings apply in several specific contexts (see (iii)–(v) for other carrier categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and service timing for tariff petitions (varies with notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions seeking investigation/suspension/rejection must meet filing deadlines tied to the notice period of the tariff filing (e.g., 3 days for 7-day notices; 6 days for less than 15-day notices; 7 days for 15–29 day notices; 15 days for 30–89 day notices; 25 days for 90+ day notices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency telegraphic requests may be used within time limits and must be confirmed by petition and served per §1.773(a)(2). See §1.773(a)(2)(i)–(v) for specific deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time and holiday rules for petitions/replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermediate holidays are counted for some filing dates and not for others per §1.773(a)(3) and (b)(2); if filing date falls on a holiday, file the next succeeding business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rules govern which deadlines count intermediate holidays and when additional mailing days apply; see §1.773(a)(3) and (b)(2) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies, service, and number of petition filings
rubrics_metrics.description: An original and four copies of each petition must be filed; distribution requires filing original + three copies with the Secretary at FCC main office and serving additional separate copies on specified bureau chiefs and the publishing carrier. Petitions on short notice have stricter personal/fax service rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.773(a)(4) for exact filing/service recipients and methods; facsimile service on the filing carrier requires same-day first-class mail follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing carrier reply timing and service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing carrier replies must be filed within specific short periods depending on the notice period (e.g., 2 days for 7-day notice tariffs; up to 8 days for 90+ day notices). An original and four copies of each reply are required and must be served on specified parties; consolidated replies may be permitted when petitions are filed on different days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.773(b)(1)–(3) for reply deadlines, computation rules, and filing/service instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing flexibility grandfathering limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Special access contract-based tariffs in effect on or before Aug 1, 2017 are grandfathered; such contract-based tariffs may not be extended, renewed, or revised except as expressly allowed by the contract. During Aug 1, 2017 through detariffing deadline, parties may, by mutual agreement, replace grandfathered contract-based tariffs with new contracts or tariffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.776 for grandfathering rules and effective date note re OMB approval; replacement options are limited and require mutual agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for extension of filing time
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension of time to file contracts, reports, and requests referred to in §§1.783–1.814 must be made in writing and may be granted for good cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.781 for request form and the 'good cause' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of carrier contracts and agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of carrier contracts, agreements, concessions, licenses, authorizations, or other arrangements shall be filed as required by part 43 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.783 for cross-reference to part 43 filing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual financial reports and SEC filing cross‑filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Telephone carriers and affiliates must file annual financial reports required by part 43 on Form M; verified copies of annual SEC reports (Form 10-K, Form 1‑MD, or equivalent) must be filed annually by each person controlling a communications common carrier in accordance with part 43.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carriers with separate carrier/noncarrier departments must file separate supplemental annual reports; see §1.785(a)–(c) and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports on proposed changes in depreciation rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers shall file reports regarding proposed changes in depreciation rates as required by part 43 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.787 for filing obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic reports regarding international point‑to‑point traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers must file periodic reports regarding international point-to-point traffic as required by part 43 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.790 for cross-reference to reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports and requests under part 32
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports and requests shall be filed periodically, upon specified events, or for specific approval by telephone companies in accordance with part 32 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.791 and part 32 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports regarding interstate rates of return (Form 492)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers shall file reports regarding interstate rates of return on FCC Form 492 as required by part 65 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.795 for the reporting obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports relating to continuing authority for international facilities (part 63)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers receiving authority under part 63 shall file quarterly or semiannual reports as required therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.802 for cross-reference to part 63 reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports relating to reduction in temporary experimental service
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers must report reductions in service that had previously been expanded on an experimental basis for a temporary period, as required in part 63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.803 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports regarding free service rendered to the Government for national defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers rendering free service in connection with national defense to any U.S. Government agency shall file reports in accordance with part 2 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.814 for the reporting obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual employment reporting (Form 395) and public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Each common carrier licensee or permittee with 16 or more full‑time employees must file an annual employment report on FCC Form 395 on or before May 31 each year. Copies of each filed report and all related documents are open for public inspection at FCC offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.815(a)–(b) for filing deadlines and public inspection; cross-references note EEO applicability for certain facilities (§25.601).
